description: Evidence-backed traits, triangulated across letters, Verne's own memoir and independent visitors (1883-1904). Only traits with at least one primary citation are included.

confidence_scale.medium: single primary source, reported speech, or unverified HTR that is legible
confidence_scale.low: uncertain reading, single ambiguous phrase, or secondary-only

records.claim: Self-described as a timid child; visitors in old age still saw a gentleness 'presque jusqu'à la timidité'; the 1855-56 letter to his father is catalogued as discussing timidity.

citations.quote: childishly timid as I was, I did not dare
Elle va presque jusqu'à la timidité
il évoque l'orgueil, la paresse, la timidité, le sens des valeurs

records.topic: work as necessity / horror of idleness
records.claim: Described work as his only true happiness and idleness as torture; kept a fixed dawn-to-11 writing routine for decades.

citations.quote: Le travail est pour moi la source du seul bonheur véritable
L'oisiveté m'est un supplice
I rise every morning before five

records.claim: Strong attachment to routine and order: read papers in a fixed sequence at the Société industrielle, classified thousands of letters, took a daily cup of milk at 3 pm at the same pâtissier.

citations.quote: le Figaro succédant au Temps, le Gaulois au Figaro
sont classées avec un soin rigoureux
sa tasse de lait quotidienne

records.topic: unambitious self-image vs. hunger for recognition
records.claim: Repeatedly called himself unambitious ('si vous saviez comme je suis peu ambitieux'), yet told Sherard his great regret was not counting in French literature (see contradictions-001).

citations.quote: si vous saviez comme je suis peu ambitieux
great regret of my life is that I have never taken any place in French literature

records.claim: Late in life signed himself 'le vieux conteur' and declared he did not deserve such praise; denied being an inventor ('I have merely made suggestions').

records.claim: Told Brisson that fishing always seemed barbaric to him and hunting horrified him; he hunted once and shot a gendarme's hat.
records.caveats: Anecdote told with evident humour; the gendarme story may be embroidered.

citations.quote: la pèche lui a toujours paru barbare et que la chasse lui inspire de l'horreur

records.topic: frugality / simple tastes in old age
records.claim: Ate eggs and greens 'as if vegetarian'; a 'buveur de lait'; ate simple meals in a small room.

citations.quote: M. Verne se nourrit d'œufs et d'herbage
Ce conquistador est un buveur de lait

records.claim: In 1854 he wrote a long 'leste et facétieuse' letter dissuading a schoolfriend from marrying.

citations.quote: Longue lettre leste et facétieuse pour déconseiller le mariage à son ancien camarade de classe

records.claim: Theatre remained central: early libretti/vaudevilles (1851 letters), detailed staging advice to directors (1874-76), lifelong theatre box in Amiens.

citations.quote: il termine un vaudeville
il parle d'Adolphe d'Ennery et de son travail sur l'adaptation du roman
I have a box at the theatre here, which I frequently occupy

records.topic: courteous, gently ironic formality toward colleagues
records.claim: As Director of the Académie d'Amiens he received new members with ceremonious courtesy ('Monsieur' repeated throughout). He paired praise with candid criticism, which he softened with self-deprecation. He called himself a near-newcomer and said it would be slightly indiscreet to ask the candidate about himself.
records.caveats: Formal public speech (written to be read aloud as Director of the Académie): a performed persona, but in his own words.

citations.quote: Vous demander à vous-même des renseignements sur vous-même, cela me semblait légèrement indiscret
au cas où je me tromperais en quelques critiques
avec ce tact parfait, cette justesse d'appréciations, et aussi cette bienveillance aimable

records.topic: love of mystification and comic hoax
records.claim: He liked staged hoaxes and comic set-pieces. In the Baril reply he tells a mock-archaeological hoax about a 'prehistoric' inscription that a schoolboy reads as dog-Latin. Une ville idéale is a whole dream-hoax set in Amiens in the year 2000.
records.caveats: Formal public speech (written to be read aloud as Director of the Académie): a performed persona, but in his own words.

citations.quote: Cellarius invenit polkam et non decorabitur
je viens de faire en rêve dans la ville d'Amiens... en l'an 2000

records.claim: Says in a public speech that he habitually rises early, which corroborates the later interviews.

citations.quote: J'ai l'habitude de me lever de bonne heure
I rise every morning before five

records.claim: He jokes at his own expense about his tax assessment ('si singulièrement coté') and the 'ruin' of paying fifteen centimes.
records.caveats: Formal public speech (written to be read aloud as Director of the Académie): a performed persona, but in his own words.
